clue.text: Gets messing about in boats

indicators.note: messing about means fooling around with something, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone gets their fun by messing about in boats on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or get hold of it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: One bird pecked another

parts.note: pecked is past tense of a beak's bite
another bird: a seabird

explanation.surface: A scene of one bird pecking another in a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to 'bird', so it means a second bird, here the tern.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading heron-family species known for its booming call.

clue.text: Put on a soft layer

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
a ply is a single layer or thickness

explanation.surface: Instructions to spread on a thin, gentle coat of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply paint or cream is to spread it onto a surface, as in putting it on.

clue.text: Foolish fellows soon led astray

indicators.note: led astray means taken off the proper path, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Silly men are quickly tempted into bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an old informal word for a simpleton or silly person, so noodles are such people.

clue.text: Military movements on the borders?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soldiers' formal walks in step
second meaning: frontier lands, as in the Welsh or Scottish border regions

explanation.surface: Troops manoeuvring along a nation's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches are the historic border districts between England and Wales or Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both soldiers' steady advances on foot and frontier territories between two countries.

clue.text: Army retreat, then change direction to do this

definitions.note: the whole clue describes the action; the verb is the answer

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the abbreviation for the army runs in reverse

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
to tack is to change course when sailing into the wind

explanation.surface: A military manoeuvre: fall back, then turn around and charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's retreat-then-turn is itself a counter-attack, which is the point of 'do this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning after a retreat to strike back at the enemy is to launch an offensive assault.

clue.text: Tribe seek to rise under many a courageous man

indicators.note: in a down entry under places one part below the other, so it comes after

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a lot
a hero is a brave man

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, so the word seek runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: A tribe strives to advance under the leadership of a brave warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American nation originally from the south-eastern United States, so the plural names its people.

clue.text: I'd fill in result — it's obvious

indicators.note: to fill in is to occupy a space inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: an event can mean an outcome, as in 'in the event'
the contraction without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they'd fill in the outcome on a form because it's plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is clearly seen or understood, a plain synonym for obvious.

clue.text: Transformation of shipmate's room?

indicators.note: read with the definition, a transformation of the words means they are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A sailor's cabin given a dramatic makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as the signal: transforming the letters of the last two words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamorphosis is a complete change of form, as of a caterpillar into a butterfly.

clue.text: Back favourites for pace

indicators.note: read as moving backwards, so the favourites word is written from end to start

parts.note: a teacher's pets are favoured pupils

explanation.surface: A punter backs the favourites in a race run at a fast pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the betting verb; it is the signal to turn the next word around.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single stride, and a pace is likewise one stride in walking.

clue.text: How the descant will be broadcast

definitions.text: How the descant will be broadcast

parts.words: How the descant will be broadcast
parts.note: surface reading: how a radio programme transmits a choir's high part
setter's reading: a descant is a melody sung above the main tune, so it sits higher than the melody

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for radio transmission also describes a descant literally: it is sung above the tune, which old musicians called the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast by radio waves is said to go out over the airwaves, while a descant literally lies above the melody.

clue.text: Stevenson's better half

parts.note: surface reading: the wife of a man named Stevenson
setter's reading: the good side of the split personality in Robert Louis Stevenson's novella

explanation.walkthrough: Better half usually means a spouse; here it is the nobler of the two selves in Stevenson's Strange Case, the other being Mr Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll is the respectable doctor whose evil alter ego is Hyde, so he is the good portion.

clue.text: Secured a routine job and set about it

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the conjunction wraps round the job phrase

parts.note: taken as written
a chore is a dull regular task

explanation.surface: Someone landed a dull steady position and got down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the routine job, so the word 'and' goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat anchored is fastened in place, so the word means fixed or held firmly.

clue.text: At the very place where one is in difficulty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: right there at the scene
second meaning: put in an awkward position, pressed for an answer

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one sentence it seems to describe a single location of trouble; the two halves are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both present at the scene and placed in an awkward or pressured position.

clue.text: For such an accident, call bronzed doctor, one from overseas

definitions.note: an adjective phrase describing the kind of accident

parts.note: hi is a greeting called out
bronzed skin is tanned, tan as adjective
standard abbreviation
un is French for one

explanation.surface: After a road accident, someone calls for a suntanned foreign doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one from overseas' means the word for one in a foreign language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run accident is one where the driver strikes someone and flees without stopping.

clue.text: Widespread issue of currency

parts.note: surface reading: money printed and circulated widely
setter's reading: currency as a flowing current, a river, whose issue is its outflow fanning out at the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Issue means outflow and currency means flow of water, so the clue describes where a river spreads out into many channels.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan-shaped area of sediment and channels where a river spreads out into the sea.

clue.text: Lad about to return stolen property

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the boy wraps around the other part

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the little word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man is about to give back things he stole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the wrapper and 'to' is the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is plunder or loot taken by thieves or soldiers, so it is stolen goods.

clue.text: In a bout we are able to last longer

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the fight word through the start of able's predecessor

explanation.surface: Boxers in a contest hope to outlast their opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to endure beyond it, as in surviving longer than a rival.

clue.text: He may get a poor press, aptly enough

definitions.note: the rest of the clue describes him

indicators.note: aptly enough hints that the phrase just given is itself the answer reworked into a fitting new order

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A man likely to receive bad newspaper coverage, and deservedly so.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no usual signal word; 'aptly enough' says the bad press fittingly holds the tyrant's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor treats people cruelly and unjustly, so he naturally earns hostile coverage from journalists.

clue.text: Fresh red rose at the back of the altar

definitions.text: at the back of the altar
definitions.note: describes where the thing stands rather than naming it

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the following letters are made anew in another order

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A newly picked red rose has been placed behind the church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel set up behind the altar in a church.

clue.text: Letters being sent to distant branch

parts.note: mail being sent goes out
letters are the post

explanation.surface: Mail is being dispatched to a remote office of the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote settlement or station, like a far-flung branch of an organisation.

clue.text: Girl is left without honour

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first pair of parts surround the honour

parts.note: taken as written
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A girl is passed over and goes without a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its older sense of 'outside', so the honour sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobel is a girl's given name, a Scottish form of Isabel.

clue.text: Prepares for action — reason may follow

parts.note: surface reading: troops readying themselves for a fight
setter's reading: the answer phrase completes an idiom when the word reason comes after it, meaning it is logical

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers on alert are said to take up position; add 'reason' to the same phrase and it means 'is logical'.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command means to take up positions ready for an attack, a standard drill phrase.

clue.text: Bridge, tailor-made for a canal

indicators.note: made means constructed, so the letters are built into a new form

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A bridge custom-built to span a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor-made' reads as one word; split it into fodder and signal. 'for a canal' points to Venice's Grand Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous stone bridge spanning the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Routed, beat a retreat

indicators.note: a routed army is scattered in disorder, so the letters that follow are scattered too

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A defeated army hurriedly withdraws from the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat a retreat' is a stock phrase, but 'retreat' stands apart as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Floodwaters or a storm that abate are said to recede or lessen, so it is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Tom's partner included on poster, say, hastily put up

parts.note: Jerry is the mouse in the Tom and Jerry cartoons

indicators.note: say means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: to be billed is to be named on a playbill or poster

explanation.surface: Jerry's name was slapped onto a hastily pasted-up poster beside Tom's.
explanation.definitionFit: To jerry-build is to construct cheaply and badly, throwing a building up quickly with poor materials.

clue.text: Eager to obtain grand ring set in silver

indicators.note: a gem set in metal is held inside it, so these parts go within the metal

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
a ring has the round shape of the letter

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to buy an impressive ring mounted in silver.
explanation.definitionFit: To be agog is to be eagerly excited and impatient, waiting to see or hear.

clue.text: Spotted end of rein caught in piece of harness

definitions.note: streaked or patchy, used of an animal's coat

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so that letter goes within the harness

parts.note: a bridle is the headgear used to control a horse

indicators.note: end of means just the final letter of the word that follows is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A horse handler notices the worn end of a rein trapped in its tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A brindle coat is grey or tawny with darker streaks or patches, as on some dogs and cattle.

clue.text: Maintains a back pressure

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word that follows reads from right to left

parts.note: stress is pressure or strain

explanation.surface: Someone insists that pressure applied to the back helps.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a view is to state it firmly, so the verb means declares or insists.
